subject: Custom SLO exhibit & DocuSign path for Veridian Health
messages:
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@veridian.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Procurement <procurement@veridian.com>, Legal <legal@veridian.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Jan 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Request: custom SLO exhibit + DocuSign flow

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers looked promising. Our procurement team reviewed the standard MSA and asked whether Redwood can provide a short SLO exhibit that captures: 99.95% monthly uptime, p50 latency <75ms (api-return), and an availability tolerance window for scheduled maintenance (no more than 8 hours/month) for the initial committed environment.

Attached is a one-page ask from our engineering team (Veridian_SLO_request_v1.pdf) that shows expected traffic patterns and a proposed rollback metric if we see >2% error burst. From procurement/legal side they also want the SLO exhibit attached to the order form rather than buried in an appendix.

Can your team:
- Confirm whether we can support the 99.95% uptime target for our Dedicated tier (RDW Dedicated Pool-E) and the latency goal for 95K tokens/day aggregated load.
- Provide a short SLO exhibit draft (to attach to the order form) and a DocuSign envelope link with the order form + exhibit so our procurement flow stays in DocuSign.

We have a target to get this into signature within two weeks. If you need more telemetry/sample traffic, we can share a small dataset.

Best,
Ethan
Ethan Cole
Director of Platform Engineering | Veridian Health
E: ethan.cole@veridian.com
T: +1 415 555 0123

Attachments: Veridian_SLO_request_v1.pdf (1 page)

From: soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@veridian.com>, Procurement <procurement@veridian.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 8 Jan 2026 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: custom SLO exhibit + DocuSign flow

Ethan — thanks for the clear ask and the attachment. Really helpful.

Quick answers up front:
- We can support a 99.95% uptime target on a Dedicated configuration, but we need to lock the capacity profile and network egress region (we recommend single-region with cross-region failover for this SLO).
- The p50 latency <75ms is achievable for typical 1–2k token responses; sustained sub-75ms for very long sequences will depend on batching/quantization settings. We will call out reasonable sequence-length limits in the exhibit.

Next steps from our side: I’ll draft an SLO exhibit that is suitable to attach to the order form (short, single page + 1 appendix for evidence & monitoring). Looping in Kar (procurement) and Naomi (legal) to confirm contract placement and redline expectations.

Kar/Naomi — can you review the Veridian attachment and let us know any mandatory legacy order-form fields (billing code, contract term, termination for convenience language) that must appear in the DocuSign envelope? Also, Naomi, do you prefer the exhibit referenced directly in the MSA or included as an attachment to the signed order form?

Ethan — I’ll get a draft to you by Monday EOD (1/12) and a DocuSign envelope suggestion the same day. If we need to push for an SLA exception (e.g., tighter latency SLAs or higher availability guarantees during peak windows) we’ll flag that and propose a fallback SLO with financial remedies.

Thanks —
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com

From: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
To: soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com, Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@veridian.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Jan 2026 08:46:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: custom SLO exhibit + DocuSign flow

Soojin / Ethan — I reviewed the Veridian_SLO_request_v1.pdf and our draft exhibit (attached: RDW_SLO-exhibit-proposal_v3.docx) includes the following negotiation points we should confirm with Veridian before finalizing the order form attachment:

1) Baseline capacity: Define committed GPU pool size (N GPUs) and a documented scaling policy. The 99.95% target is contingent on the committed pool match their traffic pattern. If they want burst capacity we should list burst reservation fees or a negotiated uplift.

2) Latency tiers: We'll propose two latency tiers in the exhibit — Tier A (p50 <75ms for up to 70% of calls) and Tier B (p95 <150ms for the remaining), with explicit sequence-length thresholds. This preserves predictable economics while meeting the spirit of the ask.

3) Maintenance windows: We recommend explicitly listing scheduled maintenance (max 8 hours/month) with a 72-hour advance notice requirement for any rolling upgrades affecting the committed pool.

4) Remedies: For availability breaches we propose service credits up to 10% of monthly invoice at defined thresholds, not termination right unless cumulative availability <97.5% over a quarter.

5) Evidence & monitoring: We'll attach a telemetry appendix describing how we compute uptime (per-tenant health checks, token-level success rate) and provide a monthly cadence for data export.

Naomi — note #4 may require legal signoff on the remedy caps and whether to expose an SLA metric that could trigger termination.

Ethan — if this approach looks acceptable I can adjust the exhibit to be an “exhibit to order form” and prepare a DocuSign packet that includes the order form + exhibit + any procurement checklist fields. Please confirm: do you want the exhibit inline in DocuSign or a separate attachment within the envelope?

-Kar
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

Attachments: RDW_SLO-exhibit-proposal_v3.docx (3 pages)

From: naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@veridian.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 10:17:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: custom SLO exhibit + DocuSign flow

Thanks — read and high level comments below. I’ll attach a redline separately to the RDW_SLO-exhibit-proposal_v3.docx and plan to remove any language that creates an easy termination/exit path tied solely to an SLO miss. Specifics:

- Remedies cap: convert the remedy to a service credit schedule with a clear definition of downtime windows; avoid any unilateral termination right tied to a single monthly breach.
- Evidence: define the canonical data export (S3 + signed CSV) and a 30-day dispute window. We should include a clause that allows for third-party audit only with mutual consent and cost allocation.
- Placement: prefer exhibit attached to the order form with an explicit reference in the order-form signature page. That keeps master terms intact while allowing the exhibit to evolve per-order.
- DocuSign technical: Procurement often needs form fields for billing code, PO number, and a signature box for auditor acceptance. If Veridian’s DocuSign envelope omits PO fields we should insert them.

I’ll send the redline and a suggested order-form template (small edits) by EOD. Kar — please keep the proposed remedy caps conservative as discussed.

-Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Quoted: On Fri, 9 Jan 2026 08:46:00 -08:00, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com wrote:

From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@veridian.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 15:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: custom SLO exhibit + DocuSign flow

Team — thanks for the quick turnaround and for surfacing practical options. Veridian is comfortable with the two-tier latency approach and the exhibit-as-order-form-attachment placement. A few asks before we send to signature:

- Please insert a PO number field and a distinct billing-code line in the DocuSign envelope so our procurement system can auto-ingest the invoice.
- Can you limit remedies to service credits (no termination right tied to a single-month SLO miss)? We agree to a quarterly cumulative availability floor for termination language if needed.
- Please send the DocuSign envelope with the order form + the redlined exhibit. We’ll complete review on our side within 24–48 hours of receiving the packet.

When you’re ready, send the DocuSign link to procurement@veridian.com and I’ll route internally. If possible, include a short cover note in the envelope reminding signatories which billing code to use and the intended contract term (12 months).

Appreciate the responsiveness.
Ethan
